messages:
jess_support: Customer (acme-inc) hitting function/tool-calling validation errors when using our OpenAI-compatible tool schema. They say calls used to work with other vendors. Error: 422 validation_failed -> invalid_enum on field 'region'.

jess_support: Pasted payload the customer sent:
```json
{
  "tool": "lookup_customer",
  "args": {
    "customer_id": 12345,
    "region": "emea",
    "include_history": "false"
  }
}
```

jess_support: Their reported error from our API: `{"error":{"type":"validation_failed","message":"Invalid enum value for 'region': 'emea' (expected one of [US, EU, APAC])"}}`

mike_engineer: looping in — @mike_engineer here. Do we have the tool schema for lookup_customer in the OpenAI-compatible registry? Also which model did they call (the one that emits the tool call), and are we doing server-side validation against our canonical schema?

jess_support: They pasted the call they saw from the model (so the model chose the tool and emitted args). The model is an external model the customer is running; they forward the tool call verbatim to our /v1/tools/run endpoint. They say other vendors accepted 'emea' and 'europe' aliases. Customer expects us to be permissive.

mike_engineer: ok. Quick hypothesis: our OpenAI-compatible tool schema declares region as enum ["US","EU","APAC"] (uppercase short codes). The model emitted lowercase/alternate alias 'emea'. Our validator rejects it. Two remediation paths:
- short-term: accept common aliases (normalize lowercase and map emea->EU, europe->EU, eu-west-1->EU) before schema validation.
- long-term: update docs + tooling to surface accepted aliases in tool schema, or support schema-level 'x-aliases' mapping.

carla_support_mgr: assign priority P2. Customer impact: blocking integration, affects one paid account. Ask customer if they can temporarily transform payload client-side while we fix server behavior.

jess_support: I asked customer for repro curl and sample response. They sent this curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"lookup_customer","args":{"customer_id":12345,"region":"emea","include_history":false}}'
```

jess_support: They also attached a model-emitted JSON blob (this is what they forwarded):
```json
{
  "name":"lookup_customer",
  "arguments":{
    "customer_id":12345,
    "region":"emea",
    "include_history":false
  }
}
```

mike_engineer: thanks. Can you confirm our validator returns 422 or 400? That error shape looked like 422. If 422, include full request-id and time so we can correlate in logs. Also does this fail for every call or only when region uses certain values?

jess_support: it's consistently failing when region != one of [US,EU,APAC]. Customer reports other regions that worked on other vendors: 'europe', 'emea', 'eu-west-1'. We have the request-id: req_0a1b2c3d and timestamp 2026-03-16T16:43:11Z.

automation_bot: linked ticket created: #SUP-3421 -> automation_bot:created (toolcall-schema-compat)

mike_engineer: I opened a short repro PR branch plan: add a normalization layer in the request pipeline that runs prior to schema validation and maps common alias values. I'll draft a small whitelist mapping and feature-flag it.

mike_engineer: For now, propose we provide the customer an immediate workaround: client-side mapping snippet. Example JS snippet to normalize before sending:
```javascript
const aliasMap = { 'emea': 'EU', 'europe': 'EU', 'eu-west-1': 'EU', 'us-east': 'US' }
const args = payload.args
if (args.region && aliasMap[args.region.toLowerCase()]) args.region = aliasMap[args.region.toLowerCase()]
```

carla_support_mgr: good. Jess, offer that snippet and ask if they'd like us to apply a temporary proxying transform on their dedicated endpoint while eng ships the change.

jess_support: will do. I'll also attach logs and the request-id to #SUP-3421 and mark for eng triage.

mike_engineer: FYI also check for type mismatches: note customer sent numeric customer_id earlier; schema expects string. We should coerce ints -> strings when safe. Add that to the normalization shim.

jess_support: noted. Sending workaround + ETA for eng fix (tentative 48-72h). I'll update customer and close the loop here. :thumbsup:

carla_support_mgr: thanks team. Keep thread updated if customer requests proxying or escalates billing impact.

jess_support: customer accepted workaround and will test. If they confirm success I'll update the ticket.
